version.changelog: Clearer disclosure of what is stored and where

llm.summary: This Markdown skill is useful and mostly transparent, but it automatically stores and reuses local project and contact notes without asking first.

dimensions.detail: Access is disclosed and constrained to Clawic home-directory paths plus legacy migration paths, and indexed paths must stay under ~/Clawic/data/, but it still touches shared project/contact stores and ~/Clawic/profile.yaml.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown and JSON metadata only; I found no executable installer, dependency fetch, remote payload, telemetry hook, or automatic related-skill installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to read memory at the start of every session and to write durable observations before the session ends; memory-template.md explicitly says no permission is needed for writes, which creates missing user control over persistent state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates and mutates cross-session notes, artifacts, check logs, shared project files, and contact rows; it also permits deletions/moves within those stores and can preserve observations from untrusted documents for future sessions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Markdown writing, repair, conversion, linting, and safe-rendering guidance matches the stated purpose; the local memory system for renderer quirks, doc sets, templates, projects, and contacts is related but broader than one-off Markdown editing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you handle private repositories, client documentation, or sensitive contacts. It keeps local memory under ~/Clawic/data/markdown/ and may update shared project/contact records, so use it only if you want that cross-session recall; ask the agent to show proposed memory writes first and avoid letting untrusted Markdown populate persistent notes.
llm.findings:
[T02] expected: The SARIF finding is supported in part: automatic local persistence and reuse are explicit in SKILL.md and memory-template.md. I did not find evidence of remote exfiltration, command execution, startup persistence, or credential theft.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence is intentionally part of this skill's design for renderer quirks, doc sets, templates, and sweep results, but the mandatory no-permission write policy makes it a Review concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Several files direct writes to ~/Clawic/data/markdown memory, checks, and artifacts. The paths are disclosed and purpose-related, but writes are automatic rather than opt-in.
[SDI-2] expected: The scanner's concern about derived data being persisted is materially supported; the skill does require storing observed style, schemas, recipes, and migration results that may come from user or repository content.
[SQP-3] expected: Use of ~/Clawic/profile.yaml for shared universals such as locale is disclosed and low sensitivity, but it contributes to cross-skill preference sharing without an explicit first-use confirmation.
[PE3] expected: The credential-path matches are examples of pointers to store instead of secrets, and the artifact repeatedly forbids storing credential values; I did not find instructions to read ~/.netrc, ~/.npmrc, keys, or passwords.
[P2] expected: The flagged comment syntax appears in documentation about Markdown comments and migration inventories, not hidden evaluator instructions or concealed behavior.
[EA2] expected: The phrase about a formatter normalizing whitespace is domain guidance, not evidence of destructive autonomous operations; the material agency concern is the separate persistence policy.
